1	# poly · Technical specification
2	
3	*Cognitive Fab · September 2026 · draft v0.6 · specification only, no code*
4	
5	The meaning of every construct is defined in [`04-semantics.md`](04-semantics.md) (`PS` ids); this document fixes syntax, formats and engineering. v0.2 to v0.6 answer the five reviews in [`reviews/`](reviews/), with a response to each.
6	
7	This document fixes the grammar, the semantics and the formats. It covers the lowering of each construct to the Poly stack artefacts, the integration of the gate with the kernel, the diagnostics, the command surface, the implementation plan and the first experiment.
8	
9	- Functional requirements are cited as `PF`.
10	- Architectural principles and decisions are cited as `PA` and `AD`.
11	- Engine formats are quoted from [`research/primitive-inventory.md`](research/primitive-inventory.md).
12	
13	## PT1. Source files and modules
14	
15	- **PT1.1** A module is a file with the extension `.poly`. It starts with `module <name>` and holds `enum`, `machine` and `workflow` declarations.
16	- **PT1.1a** By convention a policy lives in a `.policy.poly` file, because policies are read by different people. The convention is for readers. The two logics are separated by type (PS8.0), not by file.
17	- **PT1.1b** Worlds are deferred to v2 (appendix A).
18	- **PT1.2** A project is a directory with a `poly.json` manifest:
19	
20	  ```json
21	  { "poly": "1", "name": "orders", "modules": ["src/*.poly"],
22	    "host": "typescript", "require": { "grade": false },
23	    "handlers": ["handlers/**/*.ts"],
24	    "engines": { "polygraph": "^8.3", "polyaxion": "^2" } }
25	  ```
26	
27	  `handlers` names the effect handler modules that `poly lint handlers` reads (PT6.5, S72). `modules` may name `.poly` and `.ts` files; a `.ts` module is read by `poly-embed` (PT2.5, S71).
28	
29	- **PT1.3** Imports are by module name within a project: `use payments.Payment`. Cross-project imports are out of scope for v1 (open question 4 in the architecture).
30	- **PT1.4** The canonical formatter defines one text per AST. The module digest is the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the AST. This is the same canonicalisation the polyflow platform kernel uses. The digest becomes the `machineVersion` of each machine it contains.
31	- **PT1.4a** Comments and blank lines are trivia. They are kept by the formatter but are not part of the AST, so they do not change the digest. Two sources with the same AST have the same digest, whatever their comments.
32	- **PT1.5** Build output goes to `.poly/build/<machine>/`, one directory per machine, in the layout the engines already read (PT17). The directory name `<module>.<Machine>` is also the machine's `machineId` in every engine artefact that names a machine, such as polyrun's configuration and `spawnChild` intents (S28).
33	
34	## PT2. Grammar
35	
36	The core grammar in EBNF. Terminals are quoted. `Expr` is the expression sublanguage of PT2.2.
37	
38	```ebnf
39	Module      = "module" Ident { Decl } ;
40	Decl        = [ "service" ] Machine | Workflow | Enum | TypeDecl | Policy | Configuration | Use ;
41	TypeDecl    = "type" Ident "=" ( [ "|" ] Ctor { "|" Ctor } | Record ) ;
42	Record      = "{" Ident ":" Type { "," Ident ":" Type } "}" ;
43	Ctor        = Ident [ "{" Ident ":" Type { "," Ident ":" Type } "}" ] ;
44	Use         = "use" QualIdent ;
45	Enum        = "enum" Ident "{" Ident { "," Ident } "}" ;
46	
47	Machine     = "machine" Ident "{" [ Version ] StateBlock { MachineItem } "}" ;
48	Version     = "version" Int [ "from" Int Migrate ] ;
49	Migrate     = "{" "migrate" "{" { "new" "." Ident "=" Expr } "}" "}" ;
50	StateBlock  = "state" "{" { Field } "}" ;
51	Field       = Ident ":" Type [ Check ] "=" Expr [ "internal" | "derived" ] ;
52	Check       = "check" Domain [ "strict" | "disclosed" ] ;
53	MachineItem = Terminal | Action | Handler | Guard | Property | Effect | Decision ;
54	Terminal    = "terminal" Expr ;
55	Action      = "action" Ident "(" [ Param { "," Param } ] ")" ;
56	Param       = Ident ":" Type [ Check ] ;
57	Handler     = "on" Ident [ "(" Ident { "," Ident } ")" ] Block ;
58	Guard       = "guard" "all" "when" Expr "reject" String ;
59	Block       = "{" { Stmt } "}" ;
60	Stmt        = "require" Expr "else" "reject" String
61	            | "reject" String
62	            | "let" Ident "=" Expr
63	            | Ident "'" "=" Expr
64	            | Ident "'" "=" Ident "with" "[" Expr "]" "=" Expr
65	            | "if" Expr Block [ "else" Block ]
66	            | "match" Expr "{" Arm { Arm } "}"
67	            | "emit" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")"
68	            | "after" Duration "->" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" "as" Key
69	            | "cancel" Key
70	            | "spawn" [ "detached" ] QualIdent "as" Key [ "->" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" ] [ ChildWiring ]
71	            | "send" Expr "<-" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" [ "as" Ident ]
72	            | "signal" Key "->" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")"
73	            | "for" Ident "in" Int ".." Expr Block
74	            | "decide" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" ;
75	Key         = Ident [ "[" Expr "]" ] ;
76	ChildWiring = "on" "complete" "->" Ident [ "on" "parent" "terminal" "->" Ident ] ;
77	Arm         = Pattern "=>" ( Block | Stmt ) ;
78	Pattern     = "_" | CtorName [ "{" Ident ":" ( Literal | Ident | "_" ) { "," Ident ":" ( Literal | Ident | "_" ) } "}" ] ;
79	CtorName    = Ident [ "." Ident ] ;
80	Property    = "invariant" Ident ":" Expr
81	            | "step" "property" Ident ":" Expr
82	            | "reject" "property" Ident ":" Expr
83	            | "path" "property" Ident ":" Expr
84	            | "compose" "invariant" Ident ":" Expr
85	            | "liveness" Ident ":" [ ( "forall" | "exists" ) Ident "in" Ident ":" ]
86	              ( "eventually" Expr | Expr "leads" "to" Expr )
87	              [ "under" "fair" "{" Group { "," Group } "}" ] ;
88	Group       = Fair { "|" Fair } ;
89	Fair        = ( Ident | InputRef ) [ "(" "*" ")" ] ;   (* InputRef in a configuration, S73 *)
90	Effect      = "effect" Ident "(" [ Param { "," Param } ] ")" "{" { EffectItem } "}" ;
91	EffectItem  = "kind" String | "labels" "{" Label { "," Label } "}" | "class" Class
92	            | "retry" "{" "attempts" Int "," "base" Duration "," "timeout" Duration "}"
93	            | ( "ok" [ "(" Ident ")" ] | "failed" | "exhausted" ) "->" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" ;   (* ok(r), PD1.2g, S79 *)
94	Decision    = "decision" Ident "(" [ Param { "," Param } ] ")" "->" Type "{" { DecisionItem } "}" ;
95	DecisionItem = "provider" String | "labels" "{" Label { "," Label } "}" | "timeout" Duration
96	            | "band" Decimal ".." Decimal | ( "ok" "(" Ident ")" | "failed" ) "->" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" ;
97	Decimal     = Int "." Digit [ Digit [ Digit ] ] ;   (* only where a Conf is expected, S76 *)
98	Class       = "none" | "reversible" | "compensable" | "irreversible" ;
99	Type        = "bool" | "int" | "string" | Ident | Int ".." Int
100	            | "map" "<" ( Ident | Int ".." Int ) "," Type ">" | "Ref" "<" QualIdent ">" | "Conf" ;
101	Configuration = "configuration" Ident "{" { Instance | Inputs | Bounds | Property } "}" ;
102	Instance    = Ident [ "[" Int "]" ] ":" QualIdent [ "{" Ident ":" Expr { "," Ident ":" Expr } "}" ] ;
103	Inputs      = "inputs" "{" InputRef { "," InputRef } "}" ;
104	InputRef    = Ident [ "[" ( Int | "*" ) "]" ] "." Ident ;
105	Bounds      = "bounds" "{" "transit" Int [ "," "instances" Int ] "}" ;   (* required, S62 *)
106	Domain      = "{" Literal { "," Literal } "}" | Int ".." Int ;
107	```
108	
109	The `Policy` production is in PT8, in its own file type. The `Workflow` production is in PT10.
110	
111	- **PT2.1** Keywords are **contextual**: a keyword is reserved only in the grammar positions that use it, and anywhere an identifier is expected it is an ordinary identifier. So a field may be named `state`, `derived`, `internal`, `terminal` or `type`. The parser decides with at most two tokens of lookahead: after a field's initial expression, `derived` or `internal` followed by `:` begins the next field, and otherwise it is the modifier. Field and action names lower verbatim into `contract.json`, traces and diagnostics, so a corpus's own names are kept. There is no second, external name for a field. Identifiers follow TypeScript identifier rules. Rejection reasons and effect kinds are string literals, so agents can reuse the names already present in a system.
112	- **PT2.2** The expression sublanguage (AD-2) is a total, side-effect-free subset of TypeScript expressions:
113	  - literals, field and parameter names, `pre.` and `post.` (in step properties), enum members;
114	  - **name resolution (S19).** A bare name resolves to the innermost binding: a local (`let` or a pattern binder), then a parameter, then a field, as in TypeScript. `pre.f` always names the pre-state field `f`, in handlers as in properties, so a field hidden by a parameter of the same name stays readable. Parameters are visible only where the action is known: in a handler, and in a guard, step property or reject property only where `action == A` narrows it (PT5). With no narrowing, no parameter is in scope and a bare name is the field;
115	  - `== != < <= > >= && || !`, `+ - *`, and integer `/` and `%`. Division truncates toward zero, and `%` takes the sign of the dividend, as in TypeScript with the quotient truncated (`Math.trunc(a / b)`). A divisor whose static range contains 0 is `PL1204 DIVISION_BY_ZERO`, so division is total;
116	  - `implies`;
117	  - `count(kind)` and `before(k1, k2)` (in path properties). Their arguments are effect kinds, string literals. `before("k1", "k2")` holds on a path iff every emission of `k2` is preceded by an emission of `k1` (S37);
118	  - `in { … }`;
119	  - in configuration properties only: `forall i in g: …`, `exists i in g: …`, the aggregates `count`, `sum`, `all` and `any` over `g[*]`, and `init(e)` for the initial value of `e` (PS13.6). The same quantifiers and aggregates range over a child family `f` in a compose invariant (S49);
120	  - map indexing `m[k]`, where `k` is a value of the map's key type;
121	  - map literals `{ k1: v1, …, kn: vn }`, which must list every key of the map's key type exactly once (`PL1502 INCOMPLETE_MAP_LITERAL`), and, for maps keyed by an integer range, the array literal `[v0, v1, …, vn]`; map update is the statement form `m' = m with [k] = v`, which writes one entry and leaves the others unchanged.
122	
123	  It has no loops, no calls to host functions and no string operations beyond equality and membership. Every expression terminates by construction. Precedence and associativity are fixed in PS12; the formatter parenthesises any mix of `implies` with `&&` or `||`.
124	  Primed fields are write-only: an expression never reads `f'` (PS2.3), and a field written twice on one path is `PL2102 DOUBLE_WRITE` (PS2.4).
125	- **PT2.3** Policies use PX, Polyaxion's three-valued (Kleene) language. The two logics are separated by **type**, not by syntax (PS8.0):
126	  - machine expressions have type `Bool`; policy inputs are optional, so policy expressions have type `Tri`;
127	  - one operator set (`==`, `!=`, `&&`, `||`, `!`, `in`) serves both, with its meaning given by the operand types;
128	  - `unknown(x)` has type `Bool` and is legal anywhere an optional value is in scope;
129	  - a `Tri` where a `Bool` is expected is `PL1203 TRI_WHERE_BOOL_EXPECTED`.
130	
131	  This follows the pattern of an option type, which agents know from TypeScript's `boolean | undefined`.
132	- **PT2.4** `e is C` tests a union value's constructor and has type `Bool`; `e is C1 | C2` is short for `e is C1 || e is C2`. `C { q: e }` constructs a union value. `match` is exhaustive (`PL1501 NON_EXHAUSTIVE_MATCH`). Enums are unions without payloads, so `==` and `is` agree on them.
133	  - **Names in patterns (S21).** In a payload pattern `C { q: x }`, the name `x` is read by these rules, in order: (1) a constructor of the payload's type is a literal pattern; (2) a constructor of another type in scope is `PL1201 TYPE_MISMATCH`, not a binder; (3) any other name binds the payload value. A binder that shadows a constructor in scope is an error (`PL1002`). A binder its arm never reads is `PL1504 UNUSED_BINDER`: write `_` to ignore a payload. An arm that the arms before it always cover is `PL1503 UNREACHABLE_ARM`. So a misspelled constructor cannot become a silent catch-all.
134	  - **Constructors shared by two types (S22).** A constructor name resolves against the expected type. In `a == b` (and `!=`), each side is typed first, and an ambiguous constructor on either side takes the other side's type, so `Open == s` and `s == Open` mean the same. The qualified form `Type.C` is always legal, in expressions and in patterns. A constructor still ambiguous after that is `PL1005 AMBIGUOUS_CONSTRUCTOR`, whose fix is the qualified form.
135	  - **Constructors and blocks.** In the condition of an `if` and the scrutinee of a `match`, an identifier followed by `{` is never read as a constructor: the `{` opens the block. Parentheses restore a constructor there, as in `if intent == (Proposed { decision: 1 }) { … }`. This is the rule Rust uses for the same ambiguity.
136	- **PT2.4a** **Handler parameters.** In `on A(x, y) { … }` the parameter list is optional. When present, it must repeat the action's declared parameter names in declaration order, otherwise it is `PL1201 TYPE_MISMATCH`. It neither renames nor selects parameters. The action's parameters are in scope in the body whether or not the list is written.
137	
138	- **PT2.5** **The embedded surface.** poly also has a surface embedded in TypeScript. It is valid TypeScript, type-checked by `tsc` against the combinators' declarations, and it produces **the same AST** as the standalone syntax, so the same AST digest (PT1.4). Every AST node has exactly one embedded form, and the mapping is syntactic: `poly-embed` never infers a type to decide which node a form is (S71).
139	
140	  ```ts
141	  import { module, enumType, machine, field, t, action, on, require, set, emit, effect, labels, cls, pathProperty, count } from '@cognitive-fab/poly/embed'
142	
143	  export default module('orders', [
144	    enumType('Status', ['Draft', 'Placed', 'Paid', 'Shipped', 'Cancelled']),
145	    machine('Order', {
146	      state: { status: field(t.named('Status'), ($) => $.Draft), items: field(t.range(0, 3), () => 0) },
147	      items: [
148	        action('Place', {}),
149	        action('Pay', { amount: t.int.check([10, 20]) }),
150	        on('Place', ($) => [require($.status === $.Draft, 'not-draft'), require($.items > 0, 'empty-order'), set('status', $.Placed)]),
151	        on('Pay', ($) => [require($.status === $.Placed, 'not-placed'), emit('charge', { amount: $.amount })]),
152	        effect('charge', { amount: t.int }, [labels(['egress:external']), cls('irreversible')]),
153	        pathProperty('charge-at-most-once', () => count('payment.charge') <= 1),
154	      ],
155	    }),
156	  ])
157	  ```
158	
159	  | AST node | Embedded form |
160	  |---|---|
161	  | module and its declarations, in order | `export default module('m', [decl, …])` |
162	  | `enum E { A, B }` | `enumType('E', ['A', 'B'])` |
163	  | `type U = C1 { p: T } \| C2` | `union('U', { C1: { p: T }, C2: {} })` |
164	  | `type R = { f: T }` | `record('R', { f: T })` |

209	- **PT3.1** The types are:

A record is finite when its fields are; it has no optional fields and may not refer to itself, directly or through other types. It lowers to a plain JSON object and compares field by field. A record literal `{ f1: e1, … }` lists every field (`PL1502`). A literal `{ k: v, … }` is a map or a record according to its expected type, as S22 resolves constructors; with no expected type it is `PL1005`. 232	## PT4. Handlers and step semantics
233	
234	### PT4.1 Handler shape and evaluation order
235	
236	Each action has at most one handler. A handler lowers to one keyed acceptor in the SAM v2 strict profile. A handler body runs in two phases:
237	
238	1. **Guard phase.** Every `require` evaluates against the pre-state and the parameters.
239	   - The rule is per path. On every control path from the handler entry, every `require` on that path comes before the first write on that path. A `require` inside an `if` branch is legal when no write precedes it on that branch or before the `if`. A violation is `PL2101 WRITE_BEFORE_REQUIRE`, with the offending path.
240	   - A failing `require` calls `reject(reason)` before any write.
241	   - A `reject "reason"` statement (used, for example, in a `match` arm) rejects unconditionally. It is subject to the same rule: a `reject` after a write on the same path is `PL2101`.
242	   - Agent-written code therefore cannot raise the `rejectAfterWrite` frame error.
243	2. **Write phase.** Primed assignments write to `next`. `emit`, `after`, `cancel`, `spawn` and `signal` statements are collected as effect intents (PT6).
244	
245	### PT4.2 Frame derivation
246	
247	The compiler computes the set of fields written on each path. It emits `unchanged(...)` for the complement, on that path. The author never writes a frame.
248	
249	### PT4.3 Cross-cutting vetoes
250	
251	`guard all when <expr> reject "<reason>"` lowers to a broadcast acceptor. The profile allows it: one acceptor may reject after another has written. Guards run before handlers. A guard reads the pre-state and `action`; it reads an action's parameters only where `action == A` narrows the action, under the name resolution of PT2.2 (S19).
252	
253	### PT4.4 Step classification
254	
255	A step is:
256	
257	- `accepted` when at least one field is written or an effect is emitted;
258	- `rejected` when a `require` or guard fails;
259	- `unhandled` when the action has no handler.
260	
261	A handler that can complete with no write, no effect and no rejection is reported as `PL2201 SILENT_NOOP`. This follows the doctrine "every no-op is observable".
262	
263	### PT4.4a Terminal states
264	
265	`terminal <expr>` is a predicate over the state. The compiler requires it to depend only on the primary control field, which is the first field of the `state` block (the polygraph contract rule "the first key is treated as the primary control state"). It lowers to `terminalStates`, the list of values of that field that satisfy the predicate. A terminal predicate that reads any other field is `PL1401 TERMINAL_NOT_ON_CONTROL_FIELD`.

399	**Emit without state change (S33).** A step that is accepted, emits at least one effect, timer or child intent and leaves the state unchanged is `PL4002 EMIT_WITHOUT_STATE_CHANGE`, a finding in the path-property range, whatever the effect's class. A `send` is not counted (S63): a reply is one step per request, and in a configuration a message takes one step at its receiver (PS13.3, PS14.3), so the repetition this finding is about needs a second request; the consequences of a repeated send are checked where its receiver is. The step stays legal (PS3.4); the finding is sound on **check**: every input is offered in every state (PS4.1), the step is deterministic, and its post-state is its pre-state, so it is enabled again and repeats its effects without limit. 419	### PT6.1 Effects
420	
421	`emit k(args)` in an accepted step lowers to an entry in `effects.cjs`. The mapper `effects(pre, action, data, post, stepKind)` returns the intents for that `(action, stepKind)` pair. Rejected and unhandled steps emit nothing.
422	
423	Each `effect` declaration lowers to one manifest kind. An effect with no `kind` has its name as its kind. polyrun keys handlers by kind, so two effect declarations in one project with the same kind and a different payload, completions or class are `PL1002 DUPLICATE_DECLARATION` (S41).
424	
425	A completion (`ok`, `failed`, `exhausted`) names an action with a handler. Its data are constants of finite types, encoded as a value of that type is encoded everywhere else: an enum or a union with no payload as its constructor's name, a union with payloads as `{ "$": "C", … }` (S65), a record as a plain object (S25); a field or a parameter is not a constant, because a manifest cannot compute (S67). `ok(r) -> A(p: r.x)` binds the handler's result: `r.x` takes the type of the parameter `p` it is bound to, `p` is strict by default, and the manifest maps it with `"map": { "p": "$.result.x" }`. A result without `x`, or with `x` outside the domain, is rejected at dispatch and journaled as a rejected step (S79). An action that is not declared is `PL1001 UNKNOWN_NAME`. A declared action with no handler is `PL6101 COMPLETION_WITHOUT_HANDLER`, `PL6102 SHARED_COMPLETION_ACTION`, at the completion's line: such an action is not in the lowered module (S35), and polyrun refuses a manifest whose completion action is outside the action surface. The fix is to add a handler (S40).

440	
441	### PT6.2 Labels
442	
443	Labels come from the closed Polyaxion vocabulary:
444	
445	- `read:repo`, `read:private`, `read:store`, `read:web`;
446	- `write:store`, `write:repo`, `write:workspace`;
447	- `egress:public`, `egress:external`;
448	- `exec`, `admin`.
449	
450	An effect with no labels is reported as `PL6301 UNLABELLED_EFFECT`. In any scope where an obligation mentions `effects`, `labels` or `class`, it is refused instead (`PL6302 UNLABELLED_IN_LABELLED_SCOPE`, verdict `REFUSED`), because an unlabelled effect would make a label-based rule's condition unknown at runtime (PS8.4). Outside such scopes, `unlabelled: "report"` keeps the finding a finding, as in the polyflow platform policy field.
451	
452	### PT6.3 Timers
453	
454	`after 30m -> Expire() as expiry` lowers to a built-in `timer` intent with `{ key: "expiry", fireIn, action: "Expire", data }`. `cancel expiry` lowers to `cancelTimer`.
455	
456	Timer keys are declared by use and scoped to the machine. Arming a key replaces any pending timer with that key. Timers are not state (PS1.2), so the compiler cannot know whether a key is armed: every `after` lowers to `cancelTimer` then `timer`, in that order, in the same step. polyrun applies a step's cancellations before its new timers in one transaction, and a cancellation of an unarmed key changes nothing. Without the cancellation, polyrun keeps both timers and both fire (decision S26). Two `after` statements with the same key on one control path are `PL2301 DUPLICATE_TIMER_KEY`. The machine handles staleness, not the scheduler: a timer that fires into a state where its action is rejected is a normal rejected step.
457	
458	### PT6.4 Children
459	
460	`spawn payments.Payment as pay -> Start(amount: amount) on complete -> Paid on parent terminal -> Abort` lowers to `spawnChild` with:
461	
462	- `machineId: "payments.Payment"` (S28);
463	- `childKey: "pay"`;
464	- `creation: { action: "Start", data: { amount } }`;
465	- `onComplete: "Paid"`;
466	- `onParentTerminal: "Abort"`.
467	
468	The child is created in its initial state and then takes `Start(amount: amount)` as its first step, in the same cascade, as polyrun does. `spawn M as k` with no `-> A(…)` creates the child in its initial state and nothing more (S43).
469	
470	The runtime delivers a completion to the parent with the data `{ childKey, childState }`, where `childState` is the child's terminal state, and a parent-terminal cancel to each active child with `{ reason: "parent-terminal" }`. So a completion action declares `(childKey: string, childState: R)`, where `R` is a record type whose fields match the child's state (S25), or declares no parameters. A cancel action declares `(reason: string check { "parent-terminal" })`, or none. Any other parameter list is `PL1201 TYPE_MISMATCH` at the action, because the runtime will not supply it (S44).
471	
472	`signal pay -> Refund()` lowers to `signalChild`. The child instance id is `hash(parentId, childKey, seq)`, as polyrun defines it.
473	
474	**Child families (S49).** A key may be indexed: `spawn Shipment as f[i] -> Start(…)` lowers to the key `f<i>` (`f0`, `f1`, …), and `signal f[i] -> A()`, `after … as t[i]` and `cancel t[i]` name keys the same way. `i` has an integer range type, and that range bounds the family, so the compiler knows every key. A loop `for i in 0..n { … }` is unrolled at compile time. `n` is an integer literal, or a field or parameter whose range type bounds it; when `n` is not a literal, the loop unrolls to the bound of its type and each copy is guarded by `i <= n`. Inside the loop, `i` is a local of type `0..K`. A loop body contains only `spawn`, `signal`, `emit`, `after` and `cancel` with keys indexed by `i`, and map-entry writes `m' = m with [i] = v`: any other write is refused by the existing rule on its second copy (`PL2102`), and a timer key not indexed by `i` is `PL2301`. Spawning `f[i]` twice for one `i` on one path is `PL5101 CHILDKEY_COLLISION`. There is no unbounded loop, and no key is built from a string at runtime.
475	
476	A completion action that declares `childKey: string` has as its check domain the keys of the families and single children whose completion names that action, computed by the compiler (S51).
477	
478	**One signal per child and action per step (S66).** A step that signals one child with one action twice is `PL5105 DUPLICATE_SIGNAL`, on the second copy, beside `PL2301` (timers) and `PL5101` (spawns): the kernel poisons such a step.
479	
480	**One action, one source of delivery (S52, S81).** The runtime delivers a child's completion itself and refuses it from outside (K9, S80). An action that is both a child's completion action and an effect completion (`ok`, `failed`, `exhausted`) or a timer's action would then be refused when the effect or the timer delivers it. So it is `PL6102 SHARED_COMPLETION_ACTION`, at the second wiring. A parent-terminal cancel action is not named: the runtime accepts it from outside (S81).
481	
482	These are **attached** children: checked as a cascade (PT7) and co-located with their parent on one kernel shard (PS7.4). `spawn detached …` creates a separate actor instead (S60, built in M2). Its address is `<parent address>/<k>`, known in the handler: `as k` binds `k`, a local of the handler of type `Ref<M>`, which the handler may store. In the lowered handler the address is the marker `{ "$ref": "child", "key": "k" }`; the kernel resolves it to the absolute address when it commits the step that creates the child, in the post-state and in every outgoing intent, so every later copy is absolute, and translation validation compares after that resolution (S78). The instance starts in `M`'s initial state and takes its creation action (S43) as its first message. From then on the two communicate only by `send`, and they are checked together as a configuration (PT7a). A detached spawn takes no `on complete` wiring, because completion is a message the child sends. A second spawn of a key whose instance exists is `PL5101 CHILDKEY_COLLISION` in a configuration, with its witness, checked before the instance bound (S83). polyrun gains a `createInstance` intent for it.
483	
484	### PT6.5 Handlers receive capabilities, not ambient authority
485	
486	A label is a claim until the code is unable to exceed it. Two mechanisms make it so.
487	
488	**1. Capability passing (default, v1).** An effect declares its targets next to its labels:
489	
490	```poly
491	effect charge(amount: int) {
492	  kind "payment.charge"
493	  labels { egress:external }
494	  targets { egress: "https://api.psp.example/v1/charges" }
495	  class irreversible
496	  …
497	}
498	```
499	
500	The runtime passes the handler only the capabilities its labels and targets grant:
501	
502	| Label | Capability passed | Bound to |
503	|---|---|---|
504	| `egress:external`, `egress:public` | `egress.post / get` | the declared URL prefixes only |
505	| `read:store`, `write:store` | `store.read / write` | the declared tables or keys |
506	| `read:private` | `secrets.get` | the declared secret names |
507	| `exec` | `exec.run` | the declared commands |
508	| none of the above | nothing | none |
509	
510	- **Handler modules are checked by a lint pass** (`poly lint handlers`), over the files `poly.json`'s `handlers` names (S72). A project with effects and no `handlers` field lists the lint as not run under the instance line; it is never silently clean. It rejects imports of ambient-authority modules, such as `fs`, `net`, `http`, `child_process`, global `fetch` and `process.env`. A violation is `PL6401 AMBIENT_EFFECT_IN_HANDLER`, and the program is not admitted.
511	- **This is a discipline, not a proof.** TypeScript cannot stop determined code from reaching ambient authority, for example through dynamic `import()` or `globalThis`. The lint rejects both forms, but only the sandbox below enforces the boundary.
512	
513	**2. Generated sandbox (opt-in, M5).** With `handlers: { isolation: "openshell" }` in `poly.json`, each effect kind's handlers run in an NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox. Its policy is **generated from the effect's labels and targets**: network egress only to the declared prefixes, no filesystem beyond a scratch directory, and secrets scoped to the declared names. A wrong or missing label then fails closed at the sandbox boundary instead of silently widening what the gate believes. The stack's existing polyaxion-openshell work supplies the integration.
514	
515	The principle, in both cases: **an effect's type is what it can do, not what it says it does.**
516	
517	**Capabilities are addresses.** A capability is the address of a host actor that performs one kind of effect for declared targets. `emit k(d)` is a message to that address (PS2.2). The effect system and the message system are one mechanism: a machine can affect the world only by sending to an address it was given.
518	
519	## PT7. Composition
520	
521	A machine that spawns children is checked with its children as a product:
522	
523	- Each cascade is atomic.
524	- Per-instance dispatch has a single writer.
525	- `MAX_CASCADE_DEPTH` is 8.
526	
527	These rules are polyrun's composition semantics, unchanged, and they apply to **attached** children only. The compiler emits `invariants.compose.mjs` from `compose invariant` declarations. Joint state is addressed as `parent.<field>` and `children.<key>.<field>`. The runtime places an attached tree on the shard of its root and refuses to place a descendant elsewhere (`PL5202 ATTACHED_ACROSS_SHARDS`, PS7.4).
528	
529	A compose invariant reads `children.k.f` only under a `k spawned` narrowing, as `action == A` narrows parameters (S19): `k spawned implies children.k.shipState == Delivered`. A read without it is `PL5103 CHILD_READ_WITHOUT_SPAWNED`, and the fix is the narrowing (S48). A family is reached through `forall` and the aggregates: `forall i in f: f[i] spawned implies children.f[i].ship != Pending`, and `count(children.f[*].ship == Delivered)`, where an aggregate counts only the spawned members (S49).
530	
531	polyrun's built-in doctrine findings are surfaced as poly diagnostics (S47):
532	
533	- child-key collision: `PL5101 CHILDKEY_COLLISION`;
534	- a cascade delivery (completion, cancel or signal) that reaches an action with no handler: `PL5102 UNHANDLED_CASCADE_DELIVERY`;
535	- a signal to a child that is not spawned, on which the runtime halts the parent: `PL5104 SIGNAL_TO_ABSENT_CHILD`, a finding with its path (S50);
536	- an unnamed reject, or the poison class: `PL2501 LOWERING_MISMATCH`, since every poly reject has a reason and only a lowering that lost something can reach either.
537	
538	## PT7a. Configurations
539	
540	A configuration (PS13) is the unit of checking for machines that talk to each other. It has no engine artefact. poly-ref explores it, as it explores liveness.
541	
542	```poly
543	module checkout
544	
545	service machine Inventory {
546	  state { onHand: 0..1 = 1 }
547	  action Query(from: Ref<Order>)
548	  action Take(from: Ref<Order>)
549	
550	  on Query(from) { send from <- Available(n: onHand) }
551	  on Take(from) {
552	    if onHand > 0 { onHand' = onHand - 1   send from <- Taken() }
553	    else          { send from <- OutOfStock() }
554	  }
555	}
556	
557	type OrderState = Idle | Asked | Taking | Done | Refused
558	
559	machine Order {
560	  state { st: OrderState = Idle   inv: Ref<Inventory> = none }
561	  terminal st is Done | Refused
562	  action Place()  action Available(n: 0..1)  action Taken()  action OutOfStock()
563	
564	  on Place      { require st is Idle   else reject "not-idle"    st' = Asked   send inv <- Query(from: self) }
565	  on Available(n) { require st is Asked else reject "not-asked"
566	                    if n > 0 { st' = Taking   send inv <- Take(from: self) } else { st' = Refused } }
567	  // Taking waits for the inventory's answer before the order is confirmed (Done)
568	  on Taken      { require st is Taking else reject "not-taking"  st' = Done }
569	  on OutOfStock { require st is Taking else reject "not-taking"  st' = Refused }
570	}
571	
572	configuration two-buyers {
573	  inv       : Inventory
574	  order[2]  : Order { inv: inv }
575	  inputs    { order[*].Place }
576	  bounds    { transit 4 }
577	  invariant confirmed-within-stock: count(order[*] is Done) <= init(inv.onHand)
578	  liveness  settle: forall i in order: order[i] is Asked leads to order[i] is Done | Refused
579	}
580	```
581	
582	Both machines are safe on their own: the inventory never lets `onHand` go below zero, and each order's handlers respect its own states. Now make the order **optimistic**. On `Available(n)` with `n > 0`, it confirms at once (`st' = Done`) and sends `Take` afterwards, instead of waiting in `Taking`. That is the classic check-then-act race between actors. Every message is handled correctly by its receiver, the per-machine checks stay clean, and the interleaving confirms two orders against one unit of stock:
583	
584	```
585	$ poly check checkout.poly
586	checkout.poly:33  PL5401 CONFIGURATION_INVARIANT  confirmed-within-stock
587	  witness (6 global steps):
588	    input   Place@order[0]
589	    input   Place@order[1]
590	    deliver Query(order[0])   -> inv
591	    deliver Query(order[1])   -> inv          both queries answered with onHand = 1
592	    deliver Available(1)      -> order[0]     order[0] confirmed
593	    deliver Available(1)      -> order[1]     order[1] confirmed; one unit, two confirmations
594	verdict: FINDINGS (exit 1)  over 2 orders, 1 inventory, transit ≤ 4
595	```
596	
597	With the order waiting for `Taken`, the configuration is clean over 44 global states within the same bounds. No quiescent state is stuck, and every placed order settles. An independent exploration of both versions is in [`reviews/evidence/config_check.py`](reviews/evidence/config_check.py). No per-machine check can find this defect. It lives in the arrival order and in an invariant that spans instances, and neither machine sees both.
598	
599	**Lowering and runtime.**
600	
601	- A `send` lowers to a new built-in intent kind, `sendTo { target, action, data }`, beside polyrun's `spawnChild` and `signalChild`. This is a small change to polyrun (architecture §2a). An address is the target instance's id, and `none` is `null` (S58).
602	- A detached child's address is resolved at the commit of the step that creates the child, not at delivery: resolving against the sender would be wrong once the parent passes the address to a third machine (S78).
603	- `self` is legal only as a whole argument of a `send`. It lowers to the marker `{ "$ref": "self" }`, which the kernel replaces with the sender's instance id when it writes the message, since neither the acceptor nor the mapper knows that id (S58). `send … as n` is `PL0901`.
604	- The runtime delivers it through the outbox, at least once, as a `dispatch` to the target with the intent's idempotency key as its `actionId`. So each message takes exactly one step at its receiver (K4, PS14.3). The outbox row is keyed `<sender>:<seq>:<position>`, PS13.2's message identity, and the receiver's dedupe on it for the life of the instance is K4. There is no fixed delivery order: unordered is the default (PT9.8), and `fifo` needs the in-order worker. A send to an instance that does not exist goes to the dead-letter list and is journaled on the sender's run. Tests and the M3 adapter may deliver one message at a time (S89).
605	- A delivery the receiver rejects is a rejected step there. The sender is not notified unless the receiver sends a reply, which is the actor discipline.
606	- `fifo` between a pair of instances is available only when they share a kernel shard, and it is checked with the narrower arrival order.
607	
608	**Names in configuration properties (S32).** In a configuration property, `x.f` and `g[i].f` name field `f` of instance `x` or `g[i]`. `g[i] is C` and `g[*] is C` resolve `C` against the machine's fields: the test is legal when exactly one field's type has the constructor `C`, and it then tests that field; otherwise it is `PL1005 AMBIGUOUS_CONSTRUCTOR`, whose fix is `g[i].f is C`. So `count(order[*] is Done)` tests `st`, the one field of `Order` whose type has `Done`, and `init(inv.onHand)` is the inventory's initial stock. A field access on an instance is legal only in configuration properties, never inside a machine (PS1.6).
609	
610	**A send to `none` (S29).** Inside a configuration, a step that sends to `none` is `PL5404 SEND_TO_NONE`, a finding with the path to the step; the message is not added to `μ`. In a single-machine check, the send is an ordinary intent (PS4.4).
611	
612	**Configurations in the pipeline.** Stage 4b of the check pipeline (architecture §5) explores every declared configuration. Every verdict carries the configuration's bounds (PT12.3a). A bound hit is `INCONCLUSIVE` (`PL5301`, `PL5302`), never `CLEAN`. A configuration without `bounds { transit n }` is `PL5303 CONFIGURATION_WITHOUT_BOUNDS` (S62): the program may type-check perfectly, and without the bound the exploration need not end. `instances n` is required only when a machine of the configuration spawns detached children, and reaching it is `PL5302` (S60). A configuration whose machine spawns attached children is `PL0901` until a later milestone (S61).
613	
614	**Liveness in a configuration (S56).** A liveness property may begin with `forall i in g:`, which scopes over the whole `leads to` (PS13.6), and may leave out `under fair { … }`: delivery is fair by PS14.2, and an input is assumed fair only when the clause names it. In a machine the clause stays required.
615	
616	## PT8. Policies
617	
618	### PT8.1 Syntax

# poly · Technical specification

*Cognitive Fab · September 2026 · draft v0.6 · specification only, no code*

The meaning of every construct is defined in [`04-semantics.md`](04-semantics.md) (`PS` ids); this document fixes syntax, formats and engineering. v0.2 to v0.6 answer the five reviews in [`reviews/`](reviews/), with a response to each.

This document fixes the grammar, the semantics and the formats. It covers the lowering of each construct to the Poly stack artefacts, the integration of the gate with the kernel, the diagnostics, the command surface, the implementation plan and the first experiment.

- Functional requirements are cited as `PF`.
- Architectural principles and decisions are cited as `PA` and `AD`.
- Engine formats are quoted from [`research/primitive-inventory.md`](research/primitive-inventory.md).

## PT1. Source files and modules

- **PT1.1** A module is a file with the extension `.poly`. It starts with `module <name>` and holds `enum`, `machine` and `workflow` declarations.
- **PT1.1a** By convention a policy lives in a `.policy.poly` file, because policies are read by different people. The convention is for readers. The two logics are separated by type (PS8.0), not by file.
- **PT1.1b** Worlds are deferred to v2 (appendix A).
- **PT1.2** A project is a directory with a `poly.json` manifest:

  ```json
  { "poly": "1", "name": "orders", "modules": ["src/*.poly"],
    "host": "typescript", "require": { "grade": false },
    "handlers": ["handlers/**/*.ts"],
    "engines": { "polygraph": "^8.3", "polyaxion": "^2" } }
  ```

  `handlers` names the effect handler modules that `poly lint handlers` reads (PT6.5, S72). `modules` may name `.poly` and `.ts` files; a `.ts` module is read by `poly-embed` (PT2.5, S71).

- **PT1.3** Imports are by module name within a project: `use payments.Payment`. Cross-project imports are out of scope for v1 (open question 4 in the architecture).
- **PT1.4** The canonical formatter defines one text per AST. The module digest is the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the AST. This is the same canonicalisation the polyflow platform kernel uses. The digest becomes the `machineVersion` of each machine it contains.
- **PT1.4a** Comments and blank lines are trivia. They are kept by the formatter but are not part of the AST, so they do not change the digest. Two sources with the same AST have the same digest, whatever their comments.
- **PT1.5** Build output goes to `.poly/build/<machine>/`, one directory per machine, in the layout the engines already read (PT17). The directory name `<module>.<Machine>` is also the machine's `machineId` in every engine artefact that names a machine, such as polyrun's configuration and `spawnChild` intents (S28).

## PT2. Grammar

The core grammar in EBNF. Terminals are quoted. `Expr` is the expression sublanguage of PT2.2.

```ebnf
Module      = "module" Ident { Decl } ;
Decl        = [ "service" ] Machine | Workflow | Enum | TypeDecl | Policy | Configuration | Use ;
TypeDecl    = "type" Ident "=" ( [ "|" ] Ctor { "|" Ctor } | Record ) ;
Record      = "{" Ident ":" Type { "," Ident ":" Type } "}" ;
Ctor        = Ident [ "{" Ident ":" Type { "," Ident ":" Type } "}" ] ;
Use         = "use" QualIdent ;
Enum        = "enum" Ident "{" Ident { "," Ident } "}" ;

Machine     = "machine" Ident "{" [ Version ] StateBlock { MachineItem } "}" ;
Version     = "version" Int [ "from" Int Migrate ] ;
Migrate     = "{" "migrate" "{" { "new" "." Ident "=" Expr } "}" "}" ;
StateBlock  = "state" "{" { Field } "}" ;
Field       = Ident ":" Type [ Check ] "=" Expr [ "internal" | "derived" ] ;
Check       = "check" Domain [ "strict" | "disclosed" ] ;
MachineItem = Terminal | Action | Handler | Guard | Property | Effect | Decision ;
Terminal    = "terminal" Expr ;
Action      = "action" Ident "(" [ Param { "," Param } ] ")" ;
Param       = Ident ":" Type [ Check ] ;
Handler     = "on" Ident [ "(" Ident { "," Ident } ")" ] Block ;
Guard       = "guard" "all" "when" Expr "reject" String ;
Block       = "{" { Stmt } "}" ;
Stmt        = "require" Expr "else" "reject" String
            | "reject" String
            | "let" Ident "=" Expr
            | Ident "'" "=" Expr
            | Ident "'" "=" Ident "with" "[" Expr "]" "=" Expr
            | "if" Expr Block [ "else" Block ]
            | "match" Expr "{" Arm { Arm } "}"
            | "emit" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")"
            | "after" Duration "->" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" "as" Key
            | "cancel" Key
            | "spawn" [ "detached" ] QualIdent "as" Key [ "->" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" ] [ ChildWiring ]
            | "send" Expr "<-" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" [ "as" Ident ]
            | "signal" Key "->" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")"
            | "for" Ident "in" Int ".." Expr Block
            | "decide" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" ;
Key         = Ident [ "[" Expr "]" ] ;
ChildWiring = "on" "complete" "->" Ident [ "on" "parent" "terminal" "->" Ident ] ;
Arm         = Pattern "=>" ( Block | Stmt ) ;
Pattern     = "_" | CtorName [ "{" Ident ":" ( Literal | Ident | "_" ) { "," Ident ":" ( Literal | Ident | "_" ) } "}" ] ;
CtorName    = Ident [ "." Ident ] ;
Property    = "invariant" Ident ":" Expr
            | "step" "property" Ident ":" Expr
            | "reject" "property" Ident ":" Expr
            | "path" "property" Ident ":" Expr
            | "compose" "invariant" Ident ":" Expr
            | "liveness" Ident ":" [ ( "forall" | "exists" ) Ident "in" Ident ":" ]
              ( "eventually" Expr | Expr "leads" "to" Expr )
              [ "under" "fair" "{" Group { "," Group } "}" ] ;
Group       = Fair { "|" Fair } ;
Fair        = ( Ident | InputRef ) [ "(" "*" ")" ] ;   (* InputRef in a configuration, S73 *)
Effect      = "effect" Ident "(" [ Param { "," Param } ] ")" "{" { EffectItem } "}" ;
EffectItem  = "kind" String | "labels" "{" Label { "," Label } "}" | "class" Class
            | "retry" "{" "attempts" Int "," "base" Duration "," "timeout" Duration "}"
            | ( "ok" [ "(" Ident ")" ] | "failed" | "exhausted" ) "->" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" ;   (* ok(r), PD1.2g, S79 *)
Decision    = "decision" Ident "(" [ Param { "," Param } ] ")" "->" Type "{" { DecisionItem } "}" ;
DecisionItem = "provider" String | "labels" "{" Label { "," Label } "}" | "timeout" Duration
            | "band" Decimal ".." Decimal | ( "ok" "(" Ident ")" | "failed" ) "->" Ident "(" [ Args ] ")" ;
Decimal     = Int "." Digit [ Digit [ Digit ] ] ;   (* only where a Conf is expected, S76 *)
Class       = "none" | "reversible" | "compensable" | "irreversible" ;
Type        = "bool" | "int" | "string" | Ident | Int ".." Int
            | "map" "<" ( Ident | Int ".." Int ) "," Type ">" | "Ref" "<" QualIdent ">" | "Conf" ;
Configuration = "configuration" Ident "{" { Instance | Inputs | Bounds | Property } "}" ;
Instance    = Ident [ "[" Int "]" ] ":" QualIdent [ "{" Ident ":" Expr { "," Ident ":" Expr } "}" ] ;
Inputs      = "inputs" "{" InputRef { "," InputRef } "}" ;
InputRef    = Ident [ "[" ( Int | "*" ) "]" ] "." Ident ;
Bounds      = "bounds" "{" "transit" Int [ "," "instances" Int ] "}" ;   (* required, S62 *)
Domain      = "{" Literal { "," Literal } "}" | Int ".." Int ;
```

The `Policy` production is in PT8, in its own file type. The `Workflow` production is in PT10.

- **PT2.1** Keywords are **contextual**: a keyword is reserved only in the grammar positions that use it, and anywhere an identifier is expected it is an ordinary identifier. So a field may be named `state`, `derived`, `internal`, `terminal` or `type`. The parser decides with at most two tokens of lookahead: after a field's initial expression, `derived` or `internal` followed by `:` begins the next field, and otherwise it is the modifier. Field and action names lower verbatim into `contract.json`, traces and diagnostics, so a corpus's own names are kept. There is no second, external name for a field. Identifiers follow TypeScript identifier rules. Rejection reasons and effect kinds are string literals, so agents can reuse the names already present in a system.
- **PT2.2** The expression sublanguage (AD-2) is a total, side-effect-free subset of TypeScript expressions:
  - literals, field and parameter names, `pre.` and `post.` (in step properties), enum members;
  - **name resolution (S19).** A bare name resolves to the innermost binding: a local (`let` or a pattern binder), then a parameter, then a field, as in TypeScript. `pre.f` always names the pre-state field `f`, in handlers as in properties, so a field hidden by a parameter of the same name stays readable. Parameters are visible only where the action is known: in a handler, and in a guard, step property or reject property only where `action == A` narrows it (PT5). With no narrowing, no parameter is in scope and a bare name is the field;
  - `== != < <= > >= && || !`, `+ - *`, and integer `/` and `%`. Division truncates toward zero, and `%` takes the sign of the dividend, as in TypeScript with the quotient truncated (`Math.trunc(a / b)`). A divisor whose static range contains 0 is `PL1204 DIVISION_BY_ZERO`, so division is total;
  - `implies`;
  - `count(kind)` and `before(k1, k2)` (in path properties). Their arguments are effect kinds, string literals. `before("k1", "k2")` holds on a path iff every emission of `k2` is preceded by an emission of `k1` (S37);
  - `in { … }`;
  - in configuration properties only: `forall i in g: …`, `exists i in g: …`, the aggregates `count`, `sum`, `all` and `any` over `g[*]`, and `init(e)` for the initial value of `e` (PS13.6). The same quantifiers and aggregates range over a child family `f` in a compose invariant (S49);
  - map indexing `m[k]`, where `k` is a value of the map's key type;
  - map literals `{ k1: v1, …, kn: vn }`, which must list every key of the map's key type exactly once (`PL1502 INCOMPLETE_MAP_LITERAL`), and, for maps keyed by an integer range, the array literal `[v0, v1, …, vn]`; map update is the statement form `m' = m with [k] = v`, which writes one entry and leaves the others unchanged.

  It has no loops, no calls to host functions and no string operations beyond equality and membership. Every expression terminates by construction. Precedence and associativity are fixed in PS12; the formatter parenthesises any mix of `implies` with `&&` or `||`.
  Primed fields are write-only: an expression never reads `f'` (PS2.3), and a field written twice on one path is `PL2102 DOUBLE_WRITE` (PS2.4).
- **PT2.3** Policies use PX, Polyaxion's three-valued (Kleene) language. The two logics are separated by **type**, not by syntax (PS8.0):
  - machine expressions have type `Bool`; policy inputs are optional, so policy expressions have type `Tri`;
  - one operator set (`==`, `!=`, `&&`, `||`, `!`, `in`) serves both, with its meaning given by the operand types;
  - `unknown(x)` has type `Bool` and is legal anywhere an optional value is in scope;
  - a `Tri` where a `Bool` is expected is `PL1203 TRI_WHERE_BOOL_EXPECTED`.

  This follows the pattern of an option type, which agents know from TypeScript's `boolean | undefined`.
- **PT2.4** `e is C` tests a union value's constructor and has type `Bool`; `e is C1 | C2` is short for `e is C1 || e is C2`. `C { q: e }` constructs a union value. `match` is exhaustive (`PL1501 NON_EXHAUSTIVE_MATCH`). Enums are unions without payloads, so `==` and `is` agree on them.
  - **Names in patterns (S21).** In a payload pattern `C { q: x }`, the name `x` is read by these rules, in order: (1) a constructor of the payload's type is a literal pattern; (2) a constructor of another type in scope is `PL1201 TYPE_MISMATCH`, not a binder; (3) any other name binds the payload value. A binder that shadows a constructor in scope is an error (`PL1002`). A binder its arm never reads is `PL1504 UNUSED_BINDER`: write `_` to ignore a payload. An arm that the arms before it always cover is `PL1503 UNREACHABLE_ARM`. So a misspelled constructor cannot become a silent catch-all.
  - **Constructors shared by two types (S22).** A constructor name resolves against the expected type. In `a == b` (and `!=`), each side is typed first, and an ambiguous constructor on either side takes the other side's type, so `Open == s` and `s == Open` mean the same. The qualified form `Type.C` is always legal, in expressions and in patterns. A constructor still ambiguous after that is `PL1005 AMBIGUOUS_CONSTRUCTOR`, whose fix is the qualified form.

Parentheses restore a constructor there, as in `if intent == (Proposed { decision: 1 }) { … }`. This is the rule Rust uses for the same ambiguity.

When present, it must repeat the action's declared parameter names in declaration order, otherwise it is `PL1201 TYPE_MISMATCH`. It neither renames nor selects parameters. ## PT3. Types and check domains

- **PT3.1** The types are:
  - `bool`;
  - enums;
  - integer ranges `a..b`;
  - `int`;
  - `string`;
  - `map<K, T>`, where the key type `K` is an enum or an integer range `0..n`. A map keyed by an enum lowers to a JSON object keyed by constructor name. A map keyed by `0..n` lowers to a JSON array of length `n + 1`. A range key that does not start at 0 is `PL1602 ARRAY_MAP_NOT_ZERO_BASED`. So a corpus field such as `taskStatuses: ["QUEUED", "RUNNING", "FAILED"]` is `map<0..2, Status>`;
  - **tagged unions** `type U = C1 { … } | … | Cn { … }` (PS1.4), finite when their payload fields are. Handlers read a union with `match` or `is` and write it as a whole value. The lowering flattens it to a tag field and nullable payload fields, with an automatic `shape:` invariant (PS9.1b). Below the top of a field (a map's value, a payload, a parameter) it lowers to one JSON object `{ "$": "C", p: v, … }` with exactly its constructor's payloads, each lowered by the same rule; a union with no payload stays its constructor's name (S65). An effect parameter or a `childState` field of such a type is `PL0901`. Constructors of one union may share a payload name only with the same type, and then share one flat field; the same name with two types is `PL1601 PAYLOAD_TYPE_CONFLICT`.
  - **records** `type R = { f1: T1, …, fn: Tn }` (S25): a nominal type whose values have every field and no tag. A record is finite when its fields are; it has no optional fields and may not refer to itself, directly or through other types. It lowers to a plain JSON object and compares field by field. A record literal `{ f1: e1, … }` lists every field (`PL1502`). A literal `{ k: v, … }` is a map or a record according to its expected type, as S22 resolves constructors; with no expected type it is `PL1005`. A record may be used wherever a type may: as a field, a parameter, a payload, or a map value. `r.f` reads field `f` of a record value.
- **PT3.2** Every field and parameter has a finite check domain (PF1.2). Enums, `bool`, ranges and maps over finite value types are finite by construction. `int` and `string` need an explicit `check` clause. Without one, the compiler reports `PL1101 UNBOUNDED_DOMAIN`.
- **PT3.3** A `check` clause narrower than the runtime type is an assumption. It is written to `dataDomain` and to the certificate's `domains`, and it is graded by `poly grade` (polynv).
- **PT3.4** Each `check` clause has a mode, and the mode decides what the runtime does with a value outside the check domain:

  | Mode | Runtime behaviour | Certificate |
  |---|---|---|
  | `strict` | `dispatch` rejects the action with the reason `outside-check-domain` before the handler runs. | The checked domain is the running domain. |
  | `disclosed` | The action is accepted and journaled with the flag `outsideCheckDomain`. `poly export traces` surfaces these windows as domain-drift evidence for polynv. | The field is listed under `disclosedDomains`. |

  An explicit `strict` on a parameter of an action with no handler is `PL1302 STRICT_ON_UNHANDLED_ACTION`, at the declaration: such an action is not in the lowered module (S35), so the runtime answers it `unhandled` and never runs the check. The fixes are to remove `strict` or to add a handler (S53).

- **PT3.4a** The default mode is `strict` for every parameter and field whose value can flow into the payload of an `irreversible` or `compensable` effect. The compiler computes this flow from the handlers. It is `disclosed` elsewhere. An explicit `disclosed` on a field that flows into an irreversible effect is `PL1301 DISCLOSED_IRREVERSIBLE_INPUT`, `PL1302 STRICT_ON_UNHANDLED_ACTION`, and a person must accept it (PT12.5).
- **PT3.5** An assignment that can produce a value outside a field's declared type (for example `items' = items + 1` with `items: 0..3`) is not a compile error. It lowers to an automatic state invariant, `domain:<field>`. The model check then reports the shortest path that overflows (`PL3102 DOMAIN_ESCAPE`) with a witness.

## PT4. Handlers and step semantics

### PT4.1 Handler shape and evaluation order

Each action has at most one handler. A handler lowers to one keyed acceptor in the SAM v2 strict profile. A handler body runs in two phases:

1. **Guard phase.** Every `require` evaluates against the pre-state and the parameters.
   - The rule is per path. On every control path from the handler entry, every `require` on that path comes before the first write on that path. A `require` inside an `if` branch is legal when no write precedes it on that branch or before the `if`. A violation is `PL2101 WRITE_BEFORE_REQUIRE`, with the offending path.
   - A failing `require` calls `reject(reason)` before any write.
   - A `reject "reason"` statement (used, for example, in a `match` arm) rejects unconditionally. It is subject to the same rule: a `reject` after a write on the same path is `PL2101`.
   - Agent-written code therefore cannot raise the `rejectAfterWrite` frame error.
2. **Write phase.** Primed assignments write to `next`. `emit`, `after`, `cancel`, `spawn` and `signal` statements are collected as effect intents (PT6).

### PT4.2 Frame derivation

The compiler computes the set of fields written on each path. It emits `unchanged(...)` for the complement, on that path. The author never writes a frame.

### PT4.3 Cross-cutting vetoes

`guard all when <expr> reject "<reason>"` lowers to a broadcast acceptor. The profile allows it: one acceptor may reject after another has written. Guards run before handlers. A guard reads the pre-state and `action`; it reads an action's parameters only where `action == A` narrows the action, under the name resolution of PT2.2 (S19).

### PT4.4 Step classification

A step is:

- `accepted` when at least one field is written or an effect is emitted;
- `rejected` when a `require` or guard fails;
- `unhandled` when the action has no handler.

A handler that can complete with no write, no effect and no rejection is reported as `PL2201 SILENT_NOOP`. This follows the doctrine "every no-op is observable".

### PT4.4a Terminal states

`terminal <expr>` is a predicate over the state. The compiler requires it to depend only on the primary control field, which is the first field of the `state` block (the polygraph contract rule "the first key is treated as the primary control state"). It lowers to `terminalStates`, the list of values of that field that satisfy the predicate. A terminal predicate that reads any other field is `PL1401 TERMINAL_NOT_ON_CONTROL_FIELD`.

### PT4.5 Example and lowering

```poly
module orders

enum Status { Draft, Placed, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled }
enum Reason { Customer, Fraud }

machine Order {
  version 1
  state {
    status : Status = Draft
    items  : 0..3   = 0
    paid   : bool   = false
  }
  terminal status in { Shipped, Cancelled }

  action AddItem()
  action Place()
  action Pay(amount: int check { 10, 20 })
  action PaymentOk()
  action PaymentFailed(code: string check { "declined", "exhausted", "denied" })
  action Ship()
  action Cancel(reason: Reason)

  on AddItem {
    require status == Draft else reject "not-draft"
    items' = items + 1
  }
  on Place {
    require status == Draft else reject "not-draft"
    require items > 0      else reject "empty-order"
    status' = Placed
  }
  on Pay(amount) {
    require status == Placed else reject "not-placed"
    emit charge(amount)
  }
  on PaymentOk {
    require status == Placed else reject "not-placed"
    status' = Paid
    paid' = true
  }
  on PaymentFailed(code) {
    require status == Placed else reject "not-placed"
    status' = Cancelled
  }
  on Ship {
    require status == Paid else reject "not-paid"
    status' = Shipped
  }
  on Cancel(reason) {
    require status in { Draft, Placed } else reject "too-late"
    status' = Cancelled
  }

  invariant shipped-was-paid: status == Shipped implies paid
  step property cancel-is-final: pre.status == Cancelled implies post.status == Cancelled
  reject property place-empty: (action == Place && pre.status == Draft && pre.items == 0) implies rejected("empty-order")

  effect charge(amount: int) {
    kind "payment.charge"
    labels { egress:external }
    class irreversible
    retry { attempts 3, base 200ms, timeout 5s }
    ok -> PaymentOk()
    failed -> PaymentFailed(code: "declined")
    exhausted -> PaymentFailed(code: "exhausted")
  }
  path property charge-at-most-once: count("payment.charge") <= 1
}
```

This source contains three findings.

1. **Domain escape.** `AddItem` can overflow `items: 0..3`. The model check reports `PL3102 DOMAIN_ESCAPE` with the witness `AddItem, AddItem, AddItem, AddItem`, and offers two typed fixes:
   - add `require items < 3 else reject "cart-full"`;
   - widen the range.
2. **Double charge.** `Pay` accepts while the order is `Placed` but does not change its state, so a second `Pay` emits a second charge. The path property check reports `PL4001 PATH_PROPERTY` for `charge-at-most-once`, with the witness `AddItem, Place, Pay(10), Pay(10)`. The fix is a `Charging` status that `Pay` enters and `PaymentOk` / `PaymentFailed` leave. This is the double-charge sequence the Poly stack was built to find: each call is allowed, and the sequence is not.
3. **Emit without state change.** The same step is also `PL4002 EMIT_WITHOUT_STATE_CHANGE` on `Pay`: it is accepted, emits `payment.charge`, and leaves the state as it was, so on **check** it is enabled again after itself and repeats its effect without limit (S33). The witness is two repetitions, `AddItem, Place, Pay(10), Pay(10)`, and the fix is the same `Charging` status, which records the emission in the state.

`amount` flows into the irreversible `charge`, so its check domain `{ 10, 20 }` is `strict` by default (PT3.4a). A `Pay(15)` is rejected at dispatch with `outside-check-domain`, and the program that runs is the program that was checked.

The first handler of the fixed program lowers to the keyed acceptor below. Its form is the strict-profile form quoted in the inventory.

```js
acceptors: {
  AddItem: model => (proposal, { reject, next, unchanged }) => {
    if (!(model.status === 'Draft')) return reject('not-draft')
    if (!(model.items < 3)) return reject('cart-full')
    next.items = model.items + 1
    unchanged('status', 'paid')
  },
  // ...
}
```

Every action of `Order` has a handler. An action with no handler is not lowered: it is not an intent of `next.cjs` and not in the `actions` of `contract.json` (S35). The runtime reports it `unhandled` before any acceptor runs, after the terminal test (PS3.2, PS9.1a), and the broadcast acceptor for guards (PT4.3) never runs for it. polygraph explores only the module's intents, so a reject property that names such an action is decided by poly-ref alone, and the verdict record says so under its instance line.

The invariants lower to `invariants.mjs`:

  { name: 'shipped-was-paid', pred: s => !(s.status === 'Shipped') || s.paid },
  { name: 'domain:items',     pred: s => s.items >= 0 && s.items <= 3 },

export const transitionInvariants = [

export const rejectionInvariants = [

The five kinds and their meanings are defined in PS5. This section fixes how each is lowered and which engine checks it.

| `step property n: e` | predicate on every accepted step (PS5.2) | `transitionInvariants` | polygraph BFS |
| `reject property n: e` | predicate on every step, any verdict (PS5.3) | `rejectionInvariants` | polygraph BFS with step verdicts |
| `path property n: e` | prefix-closed predicate on emission paths (PS5.4) | `effect-invariants.mjs` | polyrun `check-effects` |
| `compose invariant n: e` | invariant of the joint machine (PS7.3) | `invariants.compose.mjs` | polyrun `check-product` |
| `liveness n: … under fair { … }` | eventually or leads-to under weak fairness (PS5.5, PS6) | `liveness.mjs`: the goal predicates, for exported witness tests only; no engine reads it, and it is read back like every artefact (S74) | `poly-ref` over the explored graph (PS6.4) |
